title: Philadelphia Rallies for WMMR’s 29th Annual Camp Out for Hunger
summary: PHILADELPHIA, PA (Nov. 25th, 2026) — 93.3 WMMR-FM's Preston & Steve’s 29th annual Camp Out for Hunger brought listeners, volunteers and local businesses
body_markdown:
**PHILADELPHIA, PA (Nov. 25** **th** **, 2026) —** 93.3 WMMR-FM’s Preston & Steve’s 29th annual Camp Out for Hunger brought listeners, volunteers and local businesses together to collect


**1,109,222** **pounds** of nonperishable food and raise more than


**$1,132,884** for Philabundance. The drive ran Nov. 16-20, 2026, in the Xfinity Mobile Arena parking lot next to Stateside Live! in South Philadelphia, helping stock local food pantries ahead of the holidays.


Once again, Preston & Steve broadcast live from the collection site each morning as volunteers unloaded donations from cars. Local employers organized workplace collections and raised money through Philabundance’s Business Challenge, extending the drive beyond the arena. The donations support more than 300 community partners, including food pantries, that help people facing hunger across nine counties in southeastern Pennsylvania and southern New Jersey.


“Our listeners showed up with trunks full of food, and our volunteers were there to unload them,” said Paul Blake, Vice President and Market Manager for Beasley Media Group in Philadelphia. “I’m proud of Preston, Steve and everyone across our Philadelphia stations who made those five days possible. I’m grateful to the local businesses and sponsors who helped us reach more neighbors.”


The year’s Camp Out For Hunger delivered a star-studded line of live performances and special guests. The house band lineup included


Goodman Fiske and Jamison . Singer Justin Guarini joined Goodman Fiske for a live performance during Wednesday’s broadcast, which also featured a set from rock band Fuel and a visit from John McKeever and Steve Gerben of Netflix’s “Tires.” Philadelphia Eagles veteran Brandon Graham stopped by on opening day. On Friday, Craig Robinson and Kate Flannery of “The Office” reunited in the broadcast tent, and Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker joined Philabundance CEO Loree D. Jones Brown on air to talk about the drive.


“For 29 years, Camp Out for Hunger has given our listeners a way to put food on a neighbor’s table,” said Justin Chase, Chief Content Officer of Beasley Media Group. “I’m proud of our entire Philadelphia team for earning the trust that brings people back each year. That commitment to our community is part of the work they do year-round.”


For more information about Camp Out for Hunger and ways to support Philabundance, visit


[wmmr.com/camp-out-for-hunger](https://wmmr.com/camp-out-for-hunger/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) .
